title.en: Time and dates: at seven, on Monday, in May
title.sl: Time and dates (ura in datum): at seven, on Monday, in May
title.de: Time and dates (Uhrzeit und Datum): at seven, on Monday, in May
title.it: Time and dates (l'ora e la data): at seven, on Monday, in May

rule.en:
**What time is it?** — **It's seven o'clock.** Up to half past, the minutes are **past** the hour; after it, **to** the next hour: **five past seven** (7:05), **a quarter past seven** (7:15), **half past seven** (7:30), **twenty to eight** (7:40), **a quarter to eight** (7:45). Spoken British English also says **half seven** (7:30). The digital way is right too: **seven fifteen**, **seven thirty**.

**at** a clock time: **at seven**, **at noon**, **at midnight**, and **at night**. **on** a day or a date: **on Monday**, **on Saturday morning**, **on the first of May**. **in** a month, a season, a year or a part of the day: **in May**, **in summer**, **in 2026**, **in the morning**, **in the evening**. British **at the weekend**, American **on the weekend**. With **every**, **next** and **last**, no preposition: **every Sunday**.

The days and the months have a capital letter: **Monday**, **May**.

A date takes an ordinal: **first**, **second**, **third**, then **-th**: **fourth**, **fifth**, **eighth**, **ninth**, **twelfth**, **twentieth**, **twenty-first**. Write **1 May** or **1st May**, say **the first of May**. **What's the date today?** — **It's the third of June.**
rule.sl:
**What time is it?** (Koliko je ura?) — **It's seven o'clock.** (Ura je sedem.) Do pol ure štejemo minute **past** (čez) uro, potem **to** (do) naslednje ure: **five past seven**, **a quarter past seven** (četrt na osem), **half past seven** (pol osmih), **twenty to eight**, **a quarter to eight** (tri četrt na osem). Pazi: **half seven** je 7.30, pol osmih, ne pol sedmih! Prav je tudi digitalno: **seven thirty**.

**at** pred uro: **at seven** (ob sedmih), **at noon** (opoldne), **at midnight**, **at night** (ponoči). **on** pred dnevom in datumom: **on Monday** (v ponedeljek), **on the first of May**. **in** pred mesecem, letnim časom, letom in delom dneva: **in May** (maja), **in summer** (poleti), **in 2026**, **in the morning** (zjutraj), **in the evening**. **at the weekend** (ob koncu tedna), ameriško **on the weekend**. Z **every**, **next**, **last** brez predloga: **every Sunday**.

Dnevi in meseci z veliko: **Monday**, **May**.

Datum ima vrstilni števnik: **first, second, third**, nato **-th**: **fifth, ninth, twelfth, twentieth, twenty-first**. Pišeš **1 May**, rečeš **the first of May**. **What's the date today?** (Katerega smo danes?) **It's the third of June.**
rule.de:
**What time is it?** (Wie spät ist es?) — **It's seven o'clock.** (Es ist sieben Uhr.) Bis halb zählen die Minuten **past** (nach) der Stunde, danach **to** (vor) der nächsten: **five past seven**, **a quarter past seven**, **half past seven** (halb acht), **twenty to eight**, **a quarter to eight** (Viertel vor acht). Achtung: **half seven** ist 7:30, halb acht, nicht halb sieben! Digital geht auch: **seven thirty**.

**at** bei der Uhrzeit: **at seven** (um sieben), **at noon** (mittags), **at midnight**, **at night** (nachts). **on** bei Tag und Datum: **on Monday** (am Montag), **on the first of May**. **in** bei Monat, Jahreszeit, Jahr und Tageszeit: **in May**, **in summer**, **in 2026**, und anders als im Deutschen **in the morning** (am Morgen), **in the evening** (am Abend). **at the weekend** (am Wochenende), amerikanisch **on the weekend**. Mit **every**, **next**, **last** keine Präposition: **every Sunday**.

Ein Datum hat eine Ordnungszahl: **first, second, third**, dann **-th**: **fifth, ninth, twelfth, twentieth, twenty-first**. Man schreibt **1 May** und sagt **the first of May**. **What's the date today?** (Der Wievielte ist heute?) **It's the third of June.**
rule.it:
**What time is it?** (Che ore sono?) — **It's seven o'clock.** (Sono le sette.) Fino alla mezza si dice **past** (e), poi **to** (meno) con l'ora dopo: **five past seven**, **a quarter past seven**, **half past seven** (le sette e mezza), **twenty to eight**, **a quarter to eight** (le otto meno un quarto). Si dice anche **half seven**: le sette e mezza, come in italiano. Va bene anche il digitale: **seven thirty**.

**at** con l'ora: **at seven** (alle sette), **at noon** (a mezzogiorno), **at midnight**, **at night** (di notte). **on** con il giorno e la data: **on Monday** (lunedì), **on the first of May**. **in** con il mese, la stagione, l'anno e la parte del giorno: **in May** (a maggio), **in summer** (d'estate), **in 2026** (nel 2026), **in the morning** (la mattina), **in the evening** (la sera). **at the weekend**, americano **on the weekend**. Con **every**, **next**, **last** niente preposizione: **every Sunday**.

Giorni e mesi con la maiuscola: **Monday**, **May**.

La data vuole l'ordinale, non solo il primo: **the third of June** (il tre giugno). Si scrive **1 May**, si dice **the first of May**. **What's the date today?** (Quanti ne abbiamo oggi?)
